title.narrative: Effective compliance to workplace non-discriminatory policies, including for HIV/AIDS prevention and protection of infected and affected people

description.narrative: The protection of workers in Ghana is challenge and this is more for vulnerable workers. In line with this, HIV/AIDS remains a significant public health challenge in Ghana. The Ghana Aids Commission estimated that the 2023 national adult HIV prevalence in Ghana is estimated at 1.53%, with approximately 334,095 people living with HIV. This includes 316,545 adults (94.7%) and 17,550 children (5.3%). Although, the fight against HIV in Ghana has seen significant progress, but challenges persist, especially concerning disparities among different populations. The ILO intervention will support the Ghana Aids Commission, the Ministry of Employment and Social Partners to improve the regulatory framework through the revision of the HIV at Workplace Policy to promote voluntary counselling and testing (VCT) as well as self-testing especially with the working population. The policy will ensure that targeted strategies, expanding access to HIV care, and investing in public health efforts are implemented and Ghana can continue its journey towards an HIV-free generation. In addition, to strengthen the protection of workers including the workers in the informal sectors, the government of Ghana with support from the social partners and other relevant stakeholders are reviewing the OSH Law to address the contemporary issues. Furthermore, the Ministry of Employment and Labour in collaboration with the social partners are working on an OSH profile and a national OSH strategy (including the threat of health emergencies) to ensure a safe and healthy working environment to the entire workforce, including those involved in the informal economy.
